title: Microburst reserve policy and critical-path fallback framework
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Problem: During mid-cycle spikes (short, high-intensity demand bursts) we currently either over-provision across the cycle or take reactive scope cuts that destabilize downstream deliverables. Goal: Create a lightweight, repeatable "microburst reserve" policy and paired critical-path fallback framework that product teams can apply during cycle planning and mid-cycle rebalances. The policy should define how much buffer to keep (people-hours and scope), gating thresholds that trigger reserves, and a decision playbook for authorized scope cut candidates and fallback options. It must support cross-functional coordination (Eng, Design, PM) and be compatible with Dedicated/Private capacity constraints where applicable. Deliverables: 1) Written policy and decision flowchart (Confluence), 2) Triage checklist template, 3) Example reserve allocations for 3 typical initiative shapes (growth feature, platform reliability, enterprise compliance), 4) Short training doc and 1-hour runbook workshop to onboard PMs and ENG leads.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Confluence policy page created with clear thresholds and roles; 2) Triage checklist template available in Drive and linked from Console runbooks; 3) Two pilot initiatives use the policy during a simulated mid-cycle surge and record outcomes; 4) Playbook approved by ENG lead and Head of Product; 5) Authoritative list of scope-cut types and fallback stitch points adopted by at least 3 squads.
comments: 2025-11-06 - Initial draft shared in #pm-cycle-planning. PMs asked for concrete numeric examples for 3 initiative archetypes. Action: add worked examples (Maya).
2025-11-08 - Engineering review (Diego): suggested adding Dedicated capacity constraints section and linking to capacity reservation guidelines (ENG input).
2025-11-10 - Design feedback (Asha Patel): recommended building a one-page visualization for runbook to reduce cognitive load during on-call triage. Added to next draft.
2025-11-12 - Legal flagged audit trail requirement for enterprise customers operating in Private mode; added "audit checkpoint" step to playbook. (Follow-up: confirm logging format with Security.)
2025-11-15 - PM sync: Agreed to pilot on two initiatives in Dec cycle. Diego to coordinate with ENG leads for resource tagging. Maya to schedule training workshop week of 2025-12-01.

2025-11-17 - Decision: adopt conservative default reserve of 10% FTE-hours (range 8-15%) for initiatives with >6 week horizon; teams can opt for lower reserve if they provide validated capacity forecast. Approved by Head of Product (R. Lin).
decision_log: 2025-11-09 - Tradeoff: larger reserve reduces mid-cycle surprises but increases chance of idle capacity. We prefer a small, enforceable reserve (8-12%) plus strong early detection signals rather than a large blanket buffer.

2025-11-13 - Fallback tiering decided: Tier 1 (non-negotiable) - launch blockers and security; Tier 2 - nice-to-have UX polish; Tier 3 - deferred optimization/technical debt that can be slotted later. Teams must document Tier assignments at commit time.
2025-11-16 - Operational constraint: For Dedicated customers, reserve must consider committed GPU capacity. Diego to add a Dedicated compatibility appendix to the playbook.
artifacts: Example run: GitHub issue simulation repo https://github.com/redwood-inference/cycle-policies/pulls/124
risks: Operational: Teams may treat reserve as optional and spend early, undermining policy effectiveness; mitigations: automate check in Console and require reserve confirmation during commit.
Capacity: For Private/Dedicated customers, physical GPU commitments may make rebalancing harder; mitigation: map initiative-level reserves to infra-level commitments before finalizing allocations.
Communication: Poorly communicated fallback choices can create downstream rework; mitigation: require a single source of truth checklist linked from PRDs and Console runouts.
